record.entity_title: Immigration quota capped at 0.1% of population
record.fact_text: Estonia operates an annual immigration quota that limits how many aliens may settle in the country; by the Aliens Act it must not exceed 0.1 per cent of Estonia's permanent population per year, and once exhausted, further quota-bound permits are refused for that year.
record.evidence_quote: The annual immigration quota is the quota for aliens immigrating to Estonia, which shall not exceed 0.1 per cent of the permanent population of Estonia annually.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a qualifying job guarantees a residence permit. Actually a low annual immigration quota (max 0.1% of the permanent population, roughly ~1,300 people) can be exhausted, and quota-bound applications are then refused until the next year. Action: check quota-exempt routes and apply early in the year for any quota-bound permit.

record.entity_title: ICT and start-up permits are quota-exempt
record.fact_text: Residence permits for employment in an information-and-communication-technology speciality, and for employment in a start-up company, are not counted against Estonia's immigration quota, so they are unaffected when the quota is full.
record.evidence_quote: an alien who has been issued a residence permit for employment in a post in the field of speciality of information and communication technology

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the immigration quota blocks all third-country hires equally. Actually ICT-speciality roles, start-up employees, top specialists and several other categories are excluded from the quota count. Action: if the annual quota is exhausted, check whether the role qualifies as ICT/start-up/top-specialist to proceed regardless.
